stem: A nurse teaches a parent about physical-activity recommendations for a child age 6 to 17 years. Which guidance is accurate?

options.A: Aim for at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity each week
options.B: Limit activity to light exercise and avoid strengthening activities until adulthood
options.C: Aim for at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each day, with most being aerobic and vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activity included on at least 3 days each week as recommended
options.D: Use the adult target of 150 minutes per week because children do not have separate activity guidance

rationale: CDC recommends that children and adolescents ages 6 to 17 get 60 minutes or more of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity every day. Most should be aerobic; vigorous-intensity aerobic activity, muscle-strengthening activity, and bone-strengthening activity should each be included on at least 3 days per week. C is correct.
educational_objective: Teach the current CDC physical-activity recommendation for children and adolescents ages 6 to 17.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Children and adolescents 6 to 17 — 60 minutes or more daily; aerobic, vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening recommendations
source_claim_supported: Children and adolescents ages 6–17 need at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity daily; most should be aerobic, with vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activity at least 3 days weekly.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — age-appropriate health promotion and physical-activity teaching
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — child and adolescent physical activity

source_original.stem: A nurse is providing health promotion teaching to a parent about physical activity recommendations for their school-age child. Per CDC guidelines, children and adolescents should generally get:

options.A: At least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity each week, with no need for regular activity on most other days.
options.B: At least 30 minutes of light physical activity each day, with muscle- and bone-strengthening activity avoided until adulthood.
options.C: At least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily, including aerobic and age-appropriate strengthening activities.
options.D: The same 150-minutes-per-week target used for adults, because children and adolescents do not have a separate activity guideline today.

source_original.rationale: The CDC recommends that children and adolescents (ages 6-17) engage in at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous physical activity daily, including a variety of aerobic, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activities throughout the week, to support healthy growth, development, and long-term health.
source_original.source_detail: CDC child activity guideline: ages 6–17 need ≥60 min/day moderate-to-vigorous activity; vigorous and muscle-strengthening activity at least 3 days/week, with bone-strengthening activity also 3 days/week. CDC page updated 2025-12-04; reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Made the current CDC schedule explicit: ≥60 minutes daily, most aerobic, with vigorous, muscle-strengthening, and bone-strengthening activity each on at least 3 days/week. Health Promotion mapping retained.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC physical-activity guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: CDC page dated Dec. 4, 2025 and checked 2026-08-17.
audit_findings.claim_audit: CDC directly supports daily 60-minute duration plus the three-times-weekly vigorous, muscle, and bone strengthening components.

distractor_audit.A: Weekly instead of daily target is incorrect.
distractor_audit.B: Understates activity and incorrectly excludes strengthening.
distractor_audit.D: Adult weekly target does not replace child/adolescent guidance.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: C is uniquely correct for ages 6–17.
audit_findings.cueing: Exact schedule is necessary clinical content; distractors remain plausible common misconceptions.
audit_findings.blueprint: Preventive lifestyle teaching fits Health Promotion and Maintenance.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked CDC lines 36–42; C remains uniquely correct.
